hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this instance because the variable's type only mentions variables the theorem already has, and only `[UnivLE]` is omitted. The statement does not need it to elaborate. The definition `explicitSectionsComparison` does not take it: `transportedExplicitSectionsComparison_eq` omits this instance and still states a fact about it, so `transportedExplicitSectionsComparison` and therefore `explicitSectionsComparison` do not depend on it. The proof uses it only through the Mathlib lemmas `TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing'` and `TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq'`. These come from the section of Topology/Sheaves/SheafCondition/UniqueGluing.lean that assumes `[HasLimitsOfSize] [ReflectsIsomorphisms (forget C)] [PreservesLimitsOfSize]`. The lemma `explicitSectionsComparison_injective` uses it the same way, again only via `eq_of_locally_eq'`. Both facts hold without the instance, because they only need the sheaf-implies-gluing direction. If P is a C-valued sheaf on `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, then `Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf (forget C)` (CategoryTheory/Sites/Sheaf.lean) shows that `P ⋙ forget C` is a sheaf. That lemma only requires `[PreservesLimitsOfSize.{v₁, max v₁ u₁} (forget C)]`, which here is `PreservesLimitsOfSize.{u,u}`, still available. `Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSheafFor` then gives `Presieve.IsSheafFor` for the covering sieve generated by the `W x`, and this yields both the existence and the uniqueness of gluings of compatible families of elements. This applies to `F.obj l` and to the sheafification `aP`. The other steps (`exists_compact_open_local_preimage`, `exists_open_restriction_eq_of_explicitComparison_eq`, `Concrete.colimit_exists_rep`, the filtered-category arguments) already omit this instance or never need it. So the theorem stays true and provable without it. It can also be deleted together with `[HasLimitsOfSize.{u, u} C]`.

The theorem takes this instance because it mentions only C. The statement does not need it: `explicitSectionsComparison` does not depend on it, as shown by `transportedExplicitSectionsComparison_eq` and `explicitSectionsComparison_ι_naturality`, which both omit it. In the proof it is used only to satisfy the assumptions of `TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing'` and `TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq'`, directly and through `explicitSectionsComparison_injective`. The same replacement as above removes it. `Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf (forget C)` needs only `PreservesLimitsOfSize.{u,u} (forget C)` and no `HasLimits` assumption. It shows that `F.obj l ⋙ forget C` and `aP ⋙ forget C` are type-valued sheaves, and `Presheaf.IsSheaf.isSheafFor` then gives unique gluing and local equality for the cover `W` of `U`. Nothing else in the argument uses limits in C: sheafification comes from `HasWeakSheafify`, and the colimits come from `HasColimitsOfSize`. The two instances can each be deleted on their own, and also together.
